known.title: Functional: Recover from transient network failures in runner operations
Scale: Avoid querying GitHub on every runner tick
Functional: Stop polling a human merge after 24 hours
Not done: When the work is done, the runner ends and makes no recurring GitHub calls.
Plan gap: Wire the stop continuation and summary callbacks
Standard: Replacing behaviour deletes the old path, its tests and its docs in the same change
Test: After one approval, every part becomes ready for a person to merge
Test: The folder of every merged item that holds no local changes is removed
Test: When the work is done, the runner ends and makes no recurring GitHub calls.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 4
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - a coordinator follows the shipped instructions to change the local test command.
The repaired general settings guidance still sits beside the old instruction at skill.md:222 to set `fast_test` in a fix and then close it. The guide also reserves `sample_data` edits to the coordinator at line 1247 and still says to run and watch fixes at lines 251–252. If the coordinator starts a fix whose Done-when names the setting but omits `forge.toml`, then edits that file as instructed, the automatically started worker can discard the uncommitted edit through worker.py:467–472. The standard says: “Replacing behaviour deletes the old path, its tests and its docs in the same change.”
findings.title: Standard: Replacing behaviour deletes the old path, its tests and its docs in the same change

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - GitHub returns a temporary HTTP 503 while an approved part is starting.
The runner retries a failed `task start` only when its output matches `_transient`. If the pass's initial fetch succeeds but the later fetch in task.py:223–225 returns Git's usual `The requested URL returned error: 503`, that output matches none of repo.py:349–350's network markers. The failure is logged, the repo retry is cleared, and an otherwise idle runner exits without starting the part or retrying after GitHub recovers.
Adds work: retry failed runner-owned reads and starts; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Functional: Recover from transient network failures in runner operations

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Scale
Case: normal use - a land run encounters a transient failure, then its retry spends several minutes building or waiting for checks.
The retry entry remains due after the replacement land process starts. This loop consequently requests another repo pass on every tick while that process is still running. Each pass fetches origin and calls `doctor.tidy_finished` and `nextstep.startable`; doctor.py:124 and nextstep.py:263–264 make GitHub requests. A single retry can therefore produce hundreds of unnecessary requests during a long build or check wait.
findings.title: Scale: Avoid querying GitHub on every runner tick

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a land run recovers from a transient failure, reaches a human-merge pull request, and the pull request remains unmerged for a day.
Entering human-merge polling leaves the item's already-due retry entry in `retries`. At the 24-hour deadline the code removes the polling entry and marks the item quiet, but the retry remains: lines 327–329 keep requesting repo passes and line 419 prevents idle exit. Those passes continue fetching and querying GitHub indefinitely, despite the polling deadline.
findings.title: Functional: Stop polling a human merge after 24 hours

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a loaded Windows CI worker shares an account with remembered repos.
The CI case still waits only 250 ms before checking that no runner lock, build, or merge exists. A detached Python process can take longer than that to import Forge and create the lock at runner.py:190–194. If the CI exclusion were removed, all three assertions could therefore pass before the unwanted runner begins processing the ready fix. The older-pin case now waits for a runner to start and exit, but that does not prove the CI exclusion.
findings.title: Test: CI and older-release repos do not start background work

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - a runner test worker crashes on Windows while its detached runner is alive.
The process tracker installed by this test checks for `forge.runner` in `sys.argv` or `FORGE_RUNNER=1` in tests/test_runner_moves_approved_work_to_merge.py:167. The detached runner starts with Python's `-c` argument, so the code string is absent from `sys.argv`, and runner.py:197 sets `FORGE_RUNNER` only after Python startup. The runner therefore writes no owned-process marker. After a test-worker crash, the Windows leftover-process scan in tests/conftest.py:400–420 sees only those markers and can miss the still-running runner. This violates the standard: “Tests own and clean up every process they start, even after a crash.”
findings.title: Standard: Tests own and clean up every process they start, even after a crash

stop.question:
Approved work keeps moving to merge without reminders: A background runner moves approved work to merge is stuck. It should deliver: Wake and start of the runner, automatic part and fix starts, builds through `forge land` with no chat, the land lock, polling of human merges, cleanup, the end of the runner, the stub seam for STOPS, all guide text
Two rounds in a row left the open P0 standard: replacing behaviour deletes the old path, its tests and its docs in the same change in src/forge/templates/skill.md.
The worker tried: Mark runner test platform-sensitive and update tools guide test for settings-fix flow; Fix round 3 runner review findings: guide cleanup, 5xx retry, retry lifecycle, and test tracking.
Choose one: switch this item to Claude; keep Antigravity for one more round; or narrow or split it.
